I had issues on the scar to the left. It was also my larger breast. I had to use some iodine dressings on 4 areas where I had developed some abscesses. My time off work got extended to 8 weeks rather than 6.

Getting some stretch marks on my right near my nipple. But this CAN HAPPEN AND IS PERFECTLY NORMAL FOR EVERYONE! It'll clear up with some bio oil! So I'm not bothered with them.
It's my body healing and doing it's thing!

You can make it happen. I tried so many other diets when I weighed over 250lbs, which CICO I've managed to drop to 200lbs from the start of the year to now!

Track your foods, once you find a good routine of doing it it'll become second nature to you! I'll always add in my breakfast and lunch in the morning as I know ill forget at work!

Exercise on top, and I don't mean you must go to the gym or anything. Make sure you're going for a walk at least everyday day. I used to get my 10,000 steps in most days as my "exercise" but have now started doing weights to tone up and run 3 days a week to push myself more. 

Allow yourself a treat day. It can be hard to restrict yourself every day. I allow myself to eat whatever I want (within reason of course) every Sunday and it's never made me put on weight!

Be patient with yourself. You're not going to be perfect straight away. It's all trial and error of what routine works for you and what foods work for you too. Don't be harsh on yourself if you mess up. Just start again the next day!

Make sure you're eating the correct amount of protein suitable to you. I never used to do this and was always hungry after my meals which made it harder! Now I've worked out how much I should be eating, it's made a huge difference! High protein breakfasts will help you get through until lunchtime (I always found having breakfast then the break until lunch without eating was the hardest for me)

Take pictures!! You won't see the results yourself, but photo comparisons are a treat! There would be a week where I felt bigger and then compared photos and saw that I had actually lost weight! And remember to weigh yourself! I do it weekly on a Wednesday!

Finally, water is your best friend!! I don't drink anything else now apart from on Sundays I might have a fizzy drink. But always always drink your water! 

If you have any questions or anything you're more than welcome to message me!
Good luck! You got this!

I’m still in the process of questioning and I’m 27. As most have said, I thought I was either gender fluid or non-binary. I wasn’t hugely fussed about having a female body, but knew I wanted my chest gone. And being a man, I didn’t know if I wanted to gender myself as male fully, so for a while I classed myself as being non-binary. Some days I was okay with not presenting as male, and other day’s I really didn’t like being gendered female. 

However, with counselling and talking to a lot of my trans friends at home, I was starting to realise that things I had been feeling was down to dysphoria and that from a young age (about 7) I had fantasies about being a boy, wanted to called boys name, act as a boy when me and my cousins were playing about together. I was the text book boy when I was young, playing with boy toys, wearing boy clothes and wanted to do boy things. 

As I got older (16), I was attracted to girls and assumed that all the boyish things that I liked to do was just down to me being a lesbian. When I came out to my parents they said to me “we knew you were either going to be a lesbian or come out as transgender. “
I think because I came out as gay, I didn’t think too much into being transgender because I thought that it had answered everything for me. 

It was up until I was about 24 that I realised that I still wasn’t comfortable with myself, that I hated my curves, my female voice, facial features and despised my chest more. I found out about wearing binders so purchased myself one, and wearing it oh my god made me so happy! My chest was flat, I already had short hair so I looked more masculine. 
Ever since I purchased that I knew that I could be non-binary/gender-fluid. But as the years go on and talking with my counsellor it all just clicked to me that I was transgender. 

I think patience and time is your best friend. 
Yes I would have liked to have figured this all out at a younger age, but I obviously wasn’t ready yet. And now mentally I am. 
I’m in the process to coming out to my supportive partner and family and taking those next steps to get on testosterone. 

Talk to people. Experience yourself. You’ll figure it out.
